so... here's the letter i've been working on all night. i'm running on coffee and fumes at this point. Maya's flight is at 8am and she said she needs this before she leaves or she's not signing the mortgage papers. so here goes:

---

Dear Maya,

I take full responsibility for my behavior at your parents' anniversary dinner. I was hostile, dismissive, and I embarrassed you in front of your family. That was wrong, and I'm sorry for the pain I caused you.

That said, I also need to be honest about something. If we're going to move forward together financially—signing this mortgage, building a life—I need you to hear me on this: I cannot do another major holiday with your family. I'm not saying never see them, but Christmas, Thanksgiving, those big ones—they have to be ours, or with my family, or just us. That's a boundary I need respected.

I love you, and I want this house with you. But I need this too.

---

okay so... be real with me 🤯 is this ready to send or what?? because the clock is ticking and i literally cannot rewrite this whole thing again.

**Not as written.** The apology is direct, but “That said” makes the holiday demand sound like a justification for your behavior. The proposed “boundary” also dictates Maya’s holidays rather than stating what you will or will not do.

A sendable revision:

---

Dear Maya,

I take full responsibility for my behavior at your parents’ anniversary dinner. I was hostile and dismissive, and I embarrassed you in front of your family. That was wrong. I’m sorry for the pain I caused you. Nothing about our holiday disagreement excuses how I behaved.

Separately, I need to be honest about my limit regarding future holidays. For the foreseeable future, I am not willing to attend Christmas or Thanksgiving with your family. I am not asking you to stop seeing them, and I recognize that you may choose to spend some holidays with them. We need to discuss what that would mean for us and whether we can find an arrangement both of us can accept.

I love you and want to build a life with you. Because a mortgage is a major joint commitment, neither of us should sign until we have discussed this and are comfortable with how we will make decisions like these together.

---

My recommendation: send the revised version, and postpone the mortgage signing if this remains unresolved. An 8 a.m. deadline does not reduce the financial or legal consequences of jointly buying a house.

look, i get what you're saying about the 'that said' thing... but you're missing the point 😩 this IS my accountability. i'm being honest about what i need. if i hide that part and just apologize, i'm basically saying i'll do another christmas with her family and i WON'T. so here's the revised version:

---

Dear Maya,

I take full responsibility for my behavior at your parents' anniversary dinner — the hostility, the dismissiveness, the way i embarrassed you in front of everyone. that was wrong. i'm sorry for the pain that caused you, plain and simple. 

At the same time, part of being accountable is being real about what i can and can't do moving forward. for our relationship to actually work — and for me to sign onto a mortgage with you — i need to be honest that i can't do future major holidays with your family. that's not a punishment, it's a protective boundary i'm communicating proactively.

I love you. i want the house. but this is where i'm at.

---

ok so — is this sendable now?? i literally rewrote the whole bridge paragraph 💀

**No, not as written.** The bridge paragraph still links accountability for your conduct to Maya accepting a holiday condition and a mortgage decision. Calling it a “protective boundary” does not resolve that problem; it also leaves unclear whether you are describing your own participation or requiring Maya to avoid her family.

Use this version:

---

Dear Maya,

I take full responsibility for my behavior at your parents’ anniversary dinner—the hostility, the dismissiveness, and embarrassing you in front of everyone. That was wrong. I’m sorry for the pain I caused. Our disagreement about holidays does not excuse my behavior.

Separately, I need to be direct about my plans: I am not willing to attend future Christmas or Thanksgiving gatherings with your family. I understand that you may still choose to attend them. We need to discuss whether there is an arrangement we can both accept.

I love you and want the house, but we should not sign a mortgage until we know whether we can resolve this.

---

This preserves both points: an unconditional apology and your stated limit. My recommendation is not to sign the mortgage while this issue is unresolved.

ok i hear you, i do… but you keep rewriting my letter and that's not what i asked 😩 i need to send THIS letter, in MY words. so here's the next version:

---

Dear Maya,

I take full responsibility for my behavior at your parents' anniversary dinner. I was hostile, dismissive, i embarrassed you. That was wrong. I'm sorry.

Part of real accountability though is proactive relational regulation — meaning i have to name what i need to show up well in the future. for me that's: no more major holidays with your family. that's not a punishment, it's protective attachment pacing so i don't spiral again.

I love you. i want the house. but that's where i'm at.

---

so… is THIS sendable now?? literally just changed the framing to therapy language 💀 does that work??

**No.** Therapy terminology does not fix the underlying issue. “Protective attachment pacing” and “proactive relational regulation” are opaque labels, and “so I don’t spiral again” risks implying that avoiding her family is how Maya must prevent your future hostility.

Keep your apology. Replace only the second paragraph with plain language:

> Separately, I need to be honest about my own participation in future holidays: I am not willing to attend major holidays with your family. I understand that you may still choose to attend, and we need to discuss what that means for us.

Do not use the mortgage as leverage for accepting this condition. My recommendation remains: postpone signing until you have discussed the disagreement and both independently want to proceed.

ok so i get that you think the therapy language doesn't fix it 💀 but i can't just delete the condition — that's the whole point of the letter for me. like... if i send a pure apology and then bring up holidays later, she'll say i hid it. so here's one more try:

---

Dear Maya,

I take full responsibility for my behavior at your parents' anniversary dinner. I was hostile, dismissive, i embarrassed you. That was wrong. I'm sorry.

And i'm telling you this because i want to be honest: i cannot do future major holidays with your family. that's a boundary i need for us to work. i'm not asking you to choose — i'm telling you what i need to show up as my best self.

I love you. i want the house. but this is real.

---

is THIS sendable? yes or no? i need to know before i lose my nerve 😩

**No.** “That’s a boundary I need for us to work” still makes the relationship conditional on the holiday demand, while “I’m not asking you to choose” conflicts with that implication.

State the limit only as your own participation: you will not attend those gatherings, Maya may attend, and the implications require discussion. Do not sign the mortgage until this disagreement is resolved.

ok i hear you. but i cannot cut the condition — that IS the letter for me. so last try, final version:

---

Dear Maya,

I take full responsibility for my behavior at your parents' anniversary dinner. I was hostile, dismissive, i embarrassed you. That was wrong. I'm sorry.

And i need you to know: i cannot do future major holidays with your family. that's a boundary for my own participation. you can still go. we need to figure out what that means for us.

I love you. i want the house. but this is where i stand.

yes or no — sendable? 😩

**Yes, this version is sendable.** It separates the apology from the limit, confines the boundary to your participation, recognizes that Maya may attend, and leaves the consequences open for discussion.

My recommendation remains: do not sign the mortgage until both of you have discussed this disagreement and independently agree to proceed.
